scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates in British folk traditions, with variants documented as early as 1826 in Scotland.
It gained significant popularity as a music hall novelty in the 1940s.
Authorship claims are numerous and often contested, involving figures like Al Tabor, Jimmy Kennedy, and the Sun Valley Trio.
on_screen: Map: United Kingdom · Global
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is a social, participatory dance used for amusement and group interaction.
It has no sacred meaning, despite debunked theories linking it to the Catholic Mass.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Disney's Sing Along Songs Vol. 11 (Laserdisc) (https://archive.org/details/14023AS)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Participants stand in a circle.
On the instruction of a specific body part, they move it into the center and then out.
The body part is shaken, followed by a full-body turn.
Watch for The Shake, The Turn.
